'''Greg Marshall Comlink''' is a [[Dark]] constructed list published on Decipher Deck Designs.

== Deck info ==
* '''Player:''' [[Greg Marshall]]
* '''Published:''' July 1996 (Decipher Deck Designs)
* '''Format:''' [[Premiere - A New Hope]]
* '''Side:''' [[Dark]]
* '''Starting Card:''' {{CardLink|Death Star: War Room|Premiere-D-deathstarwarroom.gif}}
* '''Strategy:''' Comlink
* '''GEMP Importable deck:''' [[Media:PANH Comlink Marshall DS 1996 Designs.txt |Download]]

== Strategy ==

This deck was made with the Dark Side cards I have collected. I have only spent a little more than $100 on CCG and I have a created a perfect deck against almost any deck. Although it is a mostly offensive deck, it still works excellent. I have never lost a game with this deck, and only lost ONE battle with it. (I only lost by one.)

== Strategy ==

Strategies: Basically, this is a dark side version of a lightside CZ-3 deck. The object is to have a high ability imperial (>3) at a location with a comlink, preferably at a central location on Tatooine, where you will be doing your draining. Have MANY cards in your hand, and several troopers and force available for any trooper guards in your hand. What this means is generating as MUCH force as possible in the first few turns, and drawing all of it. Once you have a few troopers down (even as few as three!) you can start using the Full Scale Alerts to block your oponent's movement when you timer mine them, since the average destiny in this deck is around 2.5. You may wish to drop more than one mine at once, due to the low destiny of this deck.

For Draining, stationing a bunch of guards at various locations and having a 'hit crew' in Ubrikkian can be effective, the ultimate would be to have a guard at each location, a hit squad with a few biggies and the necklace to top it all off.

Obvious modifications to this deck would be addition of any 'name' characters that you own such as Tarkin or Vader, but they're not necessary. Having Tagge and Motti at least is important though due to the free deploy of troopers which is a great help. The necklace is purely icing and is not necessary. Fiddling with the amounts of interrupts and troopers is easy and can dramatically change the way the deck plays.

The main advantage of decks like this one is that they are relatively easy to build without owning many specific rares, with many easy substitutions possible. This means that it's relatively inexpensive to build. It may not win any tournaments, but the variety of possible strategies makes it fun to play.
